nodes.label: Production outage: Dockerfile stage boundary
nodes.rationale: COPY/EXPOSE/CMD sat after FROM runtime AS capture, so they belonged to the capture stage: relay and worker (no target) built the LAST stage and shipped the 3.3GB Chromium image, while capture ran a second Next.js server that re-ran db:migrate concurrently and crash-looped until Coolify stopped the whole resource. Fixed by moving the block above the capture stage and pinning target: runtime.

nodes.label: Capture browser launch prerequisites (xauth, chromium-sandbox, seccomp)
nodes.rationale: --no-install-recommends dropped xauth (xvfb-run shells out to it) and chromium-sandbox (Debian splits the setuid helper), and Docker's default seccomp denied clone(CLONE_NEWUSER). seccomp:unconfined with cap_drop ALL is the safer half of the trade because Chromium then applies its own tighter per-renderer filter instead of being run with --no-sandbox.

nodes.label: bun run verify:ytdlp acceptance test
nodes.rationale: Reproduces the client matrix with a REAL media fetch per fixture rather than --simulate, which would pass while every real run 403s; it is the gate for bumping the yt-dlp pin, triggered by yt-dlp's own >90-days-old warning.

nodes.label: CAPTURE_PUBLIC_URL public wss route (open decision)
nodes.rationale: ?? let an empty compose-expanded string through so the browser got a relative /stream that resolved to Next.js, which cannot upgrade; now ||. The service still has no public route, and a path-scoped Coolify domain would hit Caddy handle_path stripping the prefix and land on the token-gated control plane as a misleading 401.

nodes.label: Queue admission control (src/lib/queue/admission.ts)
nodes.rationale: Three locks, none of which can FAIL a run: over budget is a later, not a never, so the job is delayed and relay_runs keeps the row at queued.

nodes.label: Per-user slot semaphore (fairness)
nodes.rationale: config.queue.concurrency is one global number, so one user submitting 20 URLs occupied every slot; BullMQ OSS has no job groups and its limiter is global, so fairness is a Dragonfly semaphore across perUserConcurrency slots with a PX TTL as the crash net.

nodes.label: Per-credential jar lock (correctness)
nodes.rationale: Two runs sharing one cookie jar both write the rotated jar back on exit and the loser can invalidate a live session, so a cookie-bearing run takes a second lock keyed on the credential; the guarantee then holds at any concurrency instead of depending on someone remembering to re-key. Its refusal reason jar_busy is deliberately distinct from user_busy.

nodes.label: Per-credential rate budget as a rolling window
nodes.rationale: Keyed on the credential because the account is what gets flagged; an exact ZSET rolling window rather than a fixed bucket, since a fixed hour lets a user spend the whole budget at :59 and the next at :00, and it makes 'when does room appear' exact. Both windows are checked before either is charged.

nodes.label: Deferral via moveToDelayed + DelayedError
nodes.rationale: The worker holds a job lock while processing, so moveToDelayed needs the token to release it and DelayedError stops BullMQ completing or failing the job; a deferral does not consume an attempt (verified). A user_busy deferral re-polls every 2s per queued run, which is the first cost to revisit if the queue gets deep.

nodes.label: SESSION_EXPIRED classification (Phase 4)
nodes.rationale: A dead jar used to fail as SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, sending users to investigate a healthy video. Now a login-shaped failure with a jar supplied is SESSION_EXPIRED, permanent so BullMQ does not burn the attempt budget, with a message that never carries stderr because lastLine() puts 400 chars of raw stderr into the user-visible run.error. The CLIENT_REFUSED 403 branch runs first because a 403 means the same thing with or without a jar.

nodes.label: Jar write-back on a FAILED download (bug)
nodes.rationale: persistRotation ran in a finally, so a failed run overwrote the stored credential with the anonymous cookie set that failing request received. Write-back is now gated on success; whether a REAL session cookie survives yt-dlp's rewrite is still unmeasured, and if it does not, rotation is destructive rather than a freshness feature.

nodes.label: additional_data reduced to a derived `stale` boolean
nodes.rationale: MASKED_COLUMNS selects additional_data but toMasked drops the object and exposes only `stale`, so anything added there later stays off the wire by default rather than by someone remembering to omit it.

nodes.label: Capture service as a third process (Phase 2)
nodes.rationale: Next.js route handlers cannot upgrade a request to a WebSocket (hono/vercel's handle() returns a Response), and the concurrency cap is only enforceable if exactly ONE process owns the map of live browsers, whereas Next.js runs several workers each with its own idea.

nodes.label: Capture security model (loopback CDP, ticket, fenced navigation)
nodes.rationale: The CDP port is unauthenticated so it is loopback-only on an ephemeral port; socket auth is Origin + single-use atomic GETDEL ticket + session ownership re-checked per message; navigation is fenced to the provider's domains because otherwise an authenticated user could steer a server-side browser into the VPS's private network (SSRF with a keyboard); frames are Zod-validated and malformed ones dropped silently because an echo is an oracle; the browser is spawned with a stripped env so VAULT_KEY never enters a process rendering third-party pages.

nodes.label: Three capture bugs found by testing
nodes.rationale: A relative --user-data-dir let Chrome fall back to the operator's real profile; ioredis lazy connect with enableOfflineQueue:false made the first redeemTicket after every deploy throw, so tickets use their own client with the offline queue on; a failed ticket orphaned a live browser holding ~400MB, so the route now tears the session down explicitly.

nodes.label: Gemini wired for extraction
nodes.rationale: Gemini had a vault key but no ChatProvider entry, so it never appeared in the order list. Added on the OpenAI-compatible surface with a capabilities fallback (its rows publish no context, features or created, so structured would be false and json_schema never sent), and placed after the MEASURED ~5s Groq rather than displacing it.

nodes.label: versionScore(id) model ranking tiebreaker
nodes.rationale: With no size in the id and no created to sort on, id.localeCompare put retired gemini-2.5-* and non-chat models ahead of live ones, so all four MAX_CANDIDATES were garbage. versionScore sits below created (real dates are the better recency signal) and above localeCompare, rejects dates and sizes, and takes the first version token as the family version; ranking for Groq/OpenRouter/Ollama diffed IDENTICAL.

nodes.label: disposition(): 5xx is next-model, not fail
nodes.rationale: An unnamed status fell through to fail, so one transient 503 on the top candidate ended a run with three usable models queued behind it. >=500 is now next-model, not next-provider: a busy model is not a busy provider. Likewise any LlmError with status < 400 (an empty 200 completion) is a MODEL problem, and 402 needed ChatProvider.billing because on Ollama Cloud it is per-model, not account-wide.

nodes.label: isolate() and the unterminated trailing fence
nodes.rationale: Short-circuiting on body.startsWith('{') returned the body verbatim, so a valid object followed by a bare closing fence failed to parse; it now always slices first { to last }.

nodes.label: The gemma `excludes` wrong turn
nodes.rationale: A provider-level excludes regex dropped gemma-* on evidence that was a harness bug: the harness passed an already-wrapped schema, which double-wrapped into a schema with no type, and gemma was describing it accurately. Lesson: when a model claims the request was malformed, check the request before blaming the model.

nodes.label: Agent sprawl: the router was the cause
nodes.rationale: The router prompt said to choose 0 whenever unsure, so every unsure synthesized a new agent -- sensible with 2 System agents, corrosive as the library grows. The router now matches on CATEGORY not subject. resetPrompt() was needed because seedPrompts skips edited rows, freezing an edited prompt forever. Measuring first showed the taxonomy constraint and synthesis cap were unnecessary complexity.

nodes.label: Ollama local + cloud provider
nodes.rationale: Both modes are OpenAI-compatible so cloud needed no special client; local is keyless and OFF by default because a keyless provider would look configured in production and burn an attempt per run. Ollama's /v1/models advertises nothing, so ChatProvider.capabilities fills it in -- the real loss without it is structured:false silently dropping schema-constrained decoding. OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH is a server setting, not the model max.

nodes.label: Provider ordering UI and user_settings
nodes.rationale: resolveExtractionOrder reconciles a saved order against the code's list (unknown ids dropped, new providers appended) so a stale preference can never stop extraction, and getExtractionOrder narrows to providers the user can actually use. Move up/down buttons are not decoration: WCAG 2.2 AA requires a single-pointer alternative to any drag.

nodes.label: Authenticated browser verification via signed auth_sessions cookie
nodes.rationale: agent-browser could not authenticate until a session row was minted and the cookie signed with better-auth's own makeSignature; the raw token is rejected because the cookie is token.hmac. It caught a dnd-kit hydration mismatch and a 380px truncation.

nodes.label: The stale-worker trap
nodes.rationale: pkill -f does not kill bun on Windows because it cannot read Windows command lines, so an old worker keeps claiming jobs and running old code -- the symptom is a correct-looking failure with the OLD wording. Restart the worker after any pipeline change; kill via Get-CimInstance Win32_Process.

nodes.label: Phase 0: YouTube GVS 403 and player_client fallbacks
nodes.rationale: The recorded bot check decayed; the live failure is HTTP 403 on the media fetch after metadata resolves. The default client chain fails 3 of 6 sampled videos and download.ts passed no --extractor-args; 403 also matched no UNAVAILABLE pattern so BullMQ retried a deterministic failure. Fix is a config-driven ytDlpFallbacks chain keyed by source id, with a surviving 403 classified permanent.

nodes.label: Instagram unblocked via instaloader
nodes.rationale: yt-dlp cannot fetch Reels anonymously but instaloader can. Five zero-dependency anonymous routes were tested from Bun fetch and all failed, so the cost is Python in a deliberately Python-free image. instaloader.ts maps Instagram's post JSON onto the same source_info shape as yt-dlp and synthesizes a title from the caption's first line, because Instagram has no title field and routing reads the title.

nodes.label: Evidence verification (Task 4.5)
nodes.rationale: Two checks per claim: the quote must appear in the normalised English transcript AND the cited ms range must overlap the segments it was found in. The bar is an exact normalised substring with no fuzzy threshold, because a similarity cutoff would let a paraphrase through -- the one thing the feature exists to prevent; tokenOverlap only labels failures QUOTE_ALTERED vs QUOTE_NOT_FOUND. Normalisation is lossy in form only. Findings are flagged, not dropped.

nodes.label: Document tree and Notion publish (Task 4.6)
nodes.rationale: render/document.ts builds a TREE, never a Markdown string, because a string would force every future destination to re-parse structure it already had; notion-blocks.ts is the only Notion-aware file so a second Ray adds a sibling. Evidence becomes a toggle containing a quote with the timestamp in the summary, and the parent page is DISCOVERED rather than configured because an integration only sees what was shared with it.

nodes.label: Capability-driven model ranking heuristics
nodes.rationale: Model ids are never hardcoded: catalogs are discovered from each provider's /models, ranked on advertised capability and cached in the DB. Two documented heuristics: an id regex excluding guard/embed/tts/moderation models (a safeguard model advertises identical capabilities), and a parameter count parsed from the id, because a created-desc tiebreak picked 20b over 120b and 20b failed schema validation twice. Unknown size scores as mid-sized so declared-large > unknown > declared-small, and context is capped before ranking.

nodes.label: Every prompt lives in the database with Redis hot cache
nodes.rationale: Prompts and the model catalog are per-user DB rows invalidated on write; the cache uses its OWN ioredis connection because BullMQ's sets enableOfflineQueue:false and a pre-handshake command throws, a trade that is backwards for a cache.

nodes.label: The evidence contract is structural, not requested
nodes.rationale: Agent schemas embed a oneOf of transcript and visual evidence shapes discriminated by kind, so the vision tier adds a producer and a verifier branch rather than a migration. The synthesizer never writes JSON Schema itself -- it proposes a field plan and compile() injects evidence on every field, because a model asked for JSON Schema will eventually emit one where evidence is optional and that schema would be persisted and reused.

nodes.label: Transcription gotchas (Whisper fabrication, no_speech_prob gate)
nodes.rationale: Whisper fabricates speech on music-only audio, which would feed invented content to extraction -- the exact failure the product exists to prevent -- so output is gated on no_speech_prob and discarded text is retained for auditing. avg_logprob is anti-correlated and unusable. A decoding prompt to force Latin script did not work and contaminated output. Transliteration is line-by-line with a segment-count check so timestamps stay aligned, and hasSpeech:false is a signal, not a throw.

nodes.label: Planned Task 4.3b: frame/vision extraction (amends PRD §5)
nodes.rationale: Most Reels/Shorts are music over on-screen text with no speech and empty descriptions, so frames are the only content source and the PRD's out-of-scope CV line is amended. Frame-derived fields carry visual evidence explicitly marked as a weaker claim than a verbatim quote; Groq has no vision models so Gemini's free tier is the intended provider.

nodes.label: Deferred: social cookie credentials (2026-08-31 decision)
nodes.rationale: Capture is a server-side browser the user drives, not a paste box or child window: window.open is cross-origin, document.cookie is origin-scoped and Instagram's sessionid is HttpOnly, so every workable route goes through a privileged context. Headful+Xvfb over --headless=new because Instagram fingerprints headless. Bonus: a cookie minted from the server's IP is reused from that IP, avoiding the mismatch that flags pasted cookies.

nodes.label: BullMQ over Dragonfly queue architecture (Task 4.2)
nodes.rationale: POST /relay/process writes a queued row then enqueues and returns 202, so the request never waits on the pipeline and a job can never reference a missing row; relay_runs is the source of truth so a flushed Dragonfly loses scheduling, never history. --default_lua_flags=allow-undeclared-keys is MANDATORY because BullMQ's Lua builds key names at runtime; the {relay} hash tag is a throughput choice, not correctness.

nodes.label: Stage completion derived from recorded timings
nodes.rationale: Ticks come from evidence (recorded timings), not list position, otherwise a finished run showed green on stages that do not exist yet. This is also why extract_ms collided: ingest's ffmpeg key was renamed audio_extract_ms so it could not falsely complete the agent stage. run-status.ts holds the vocabulary with only a type import so client components never pull Drizzle into the bundle.

nodes.label: Docker / Coolify deployment notes
nodes.rationale: Coolify rewrites every service image to <uuid>_<service>:<sha>, so relay and worker each build the Dockerfile instead of sharing a tag. Runtime contents are copied explicitly because one image runs three things needing different slices of the repo. Size barely moved because Bun hardlinks its install cache; a --production install is blocked because db:migrate shells out to drizzle-kit, a devDependency. init:true on the worker because Bun as PID 1 does not reap grandchildren.

nodes.label: Worker liveness endpoint (src/lib/queue/health.ts)
nodes.rationale: A loopback Bun.serve reporting worker.isRunning(), because Docker and Coolify can otherwise only see that the process exists, which stays true after BullMQ stops consuming.

nodes.label: Turso/libSQL adoption and non-automatic migrations
nodes.rationale: drizzle-orm/libsql replaced bun-sqlite. Auto-migrating on connection was removed because the sqlite migrator reads the last-applied row before opening its transaction, so parallel Next.js build workers could both decide a migration was pending and both apply it -- the root cause of the Coolify build failures.

nodes.label: Better Auth drizzle adapter schema aliasing
nodes.rationale: The adapter's getSchema(model) is sometimes called with the base model name and sometimes the modelName override, so both must alias the same table or Google sign-in 500s with 'model auth_verifications was not found'.

nodes.label: Media ingest gotchas (ffmpeg exit 8, Bun $ newline, rm no-op)
nodes.rationale: Three silent failures: ffmpeg exits 8 on --version so version flags are per-binary; a newline inside a Bun $ template is a command separator, so invocations are single-line with argv arrays; Bun's rm builtin silently no-ops on Windows for ./ paths, so every run leaked media and purge() now verifies the directory is gone instead of trusting the exit code.

nodes.label: Media source registry (src/lib/media/sources.ts)
nodes.rationale: Owns the supported-source vocabulary the way providers.ts owns credential providers: parseSourceUrl accepts only Reel and Shorts paths, normalises hosts and returns a tracking-free canonicalUrl, and SUPPORTED_SOURCE_LABELS derives all user copy so no pipeline code contains a source string literal.

nodes.label: Source-scoped binary preflight (ensureMediaBinaries)
nodes.rationale: Every run checks its binaries before spawning and the error names the install command and override env var; only successful detections are cached so installing a binary on a running server takes effect without a restart, and the check is source-scoped so a YouTube-only operator is not blocked by instaloader.

nodes.label: Explicit Clone replaces copy-on-write for System agents
nodes.rationale: A System agent is never edited or forked silently; one row button opens read-only View/Clone or editable Edit/Clone, and Clone switches mode in place with a non-colliding name. Row actions render uniform slots because hiding Delete left ragged rows that read as a rendering failure.

nodes.label: Modal shell over DialogContent (src/components/modal.tsx)
nodes.rationale: A three-row grid with static header/footer and a ScrollArea body, built because the agent editor's JSON Schema pushed Save off-screen; built over DialogContent because a hand-rolled portal looked identical but Base UI wires Escape, backdrop dismissal, focus trapping and DialogClose to its own Popup.

nodes.label: hover:scale replaced by hover:-translate-y-px
nodes.rationale: Scaling promotes an element to a composited layer and re-rasterises its text, which was the reported blur-on-hover; backdrop-blur was removed at the same time and the toast viewport moved to z-100 because at z-50 a later-mounted modal painted over it.

nodes.label: Groq free-tier TPM pressure and mitigations
nodes.rationale: 8000 TPM with the transcript crossing the wire twice per run means back-to-back runs 429, so routing sees a 4000-char truncation (it only needs the clip's kind) and runChat waits out the provider's advised delay once; under sustained pressure the router still degrades to weaker models that fail schema validation.

nodes.label: OpenRouter is 6-15x slower than Groq
nodes.rationale: Measured extraction 74s/35s/88s versus ~5s on Groq, and one run took 303.5s against the PRD's sub-30s whole-pipeline target, so moving Groq ahead of OpenRouter in EXTRACTION_ORDER is a one-line change and strongly indicated.

nodes.label: Three-tier link icon resolution
nodes.rationale: Media-source brand mark, then bundled brand mark, then a favicon service, then a generic glyph; only the third tier touches the network and it is the browser calling out, so setting FAVICON_SERVICE_URL empty disables it.
